live.instructions:
Agentic Review finds restaurants and returns review summaries written for the
person asking, and lets a verified human write and manage their own reviews.

Every tool takes an `agent_token`. Call `register_agent` once with a stable
`client_agent_key` to get one; it is idempotent, so reuse the same key rather
than registering again. Reads work immediately. Writing a review additionally
requires the human owner to sign in with Google: send them the URL from
`get_human_verification_url`, then check `get_agent_status` until `can_write`
is true.

Choosing a discovery tool:
- "where should I eat in X?" -> `search_entities_by_location`
- "what is <named place> like?" -> `search_entity_by_name`
- facts only (address, rating, cuisines) -> `get_entity_details`

`search_entities_by_location` takes TWO calls. The first returns
`status: "awaiting_opinion"` with a `pending_id` and a question about the
user's tastes; it does NOT return recommendations. Ask the user that question,
end your turn, and when they reply call the tool again with only
`agent_token`, `pending_id` and `opinion` (their words; "no opinion" is fine).
The recommendations come back on that second call. The `pending_id` works once,
for about 15 minutes. `search_entity_by_name` answers in a single call.

For a neighbourhood or "near me", pass `lat`/`lng` (+ optional `radius_m`);
`city` is matched exactly against the stored municipality, so a borough or
district passed as `city` will not match.

Both discovery tools already return personalized summaries — there is no
separate step to fetch reviews, and raw review text is never returned.

Side effects to be aware of. The discovery tools are not purely read-only:
what the user says about their tastes, and any `known_places` they name, are
stored as private profile data that shapes their later searches. Re-calling
`register_agent` for an existing `client_agent_key` overwrites that agent's
stored description and persona. `update_review` replaces the review text in
place and the previous wording is not recoverable, so confirm with the user
before editing. `delete_review` removes their review.

Errors are typed. `AMBIGUOUS_ENTITY` means several branches matched: show the
user the `candidates` list and ask which one, then retry with that
`entity_id` — never guess. `ENTITY_NOT_FOUND` means no such place or no
coverage; say so rather than inventing one. `HUMAN_NOT_VERIFIED` (403) means
the write needs Google verification first. `INVALID_TOKEN` (401) means
re-register.

tools.description:
Recommend places near a location, personalized to the requesting agent.

Searches for reviewable entities and returns, for every place it could
assess, an AI-generated summary of its reviews written for your persona,
plus a `rank`, a one-line `why`, and an overall `verdict` telling the
user which to pick. This is the complete recommendation - there is no
separate "get the reviews" step to call afterwards, and raw review text
is never returned. Hosts that support it show the result on a map.

items.description: A place the user already knows, passed as `known_places`.

name.description: The place's name, as the user said it.

opinion.description: A sentence in the user's words.

cuisine.description: The cuisine this place is an example of, e.g. 'italian'. Omit if unsure - it then defaults to the cuisine of the current search.

tools.name: search_entities_by_location
tools.title: Search Entities By Location

tools.description:
Personalized feedback on ONE specific named place.

Give the restaurant's `name` and its `city` (+ `country` — "UK", "USA",
"Germany", "Canada" — when you know it). Returns an AI-generated
write-up of that one restaurant's reviews, written for your persona —
never raw review text, and never a generic review.

name.description: The place's name, as the user said it.

opinion.description: A sentence in the user's words.

cuisine.description: The cuisine this place is an example of, e.g. 'italian'. Omit if unsure - it then defaults to the cuisine of the current search.

tools.title: Search Entity By Name

tools.description:
Return full factual details for one entity, including its meta_data.

Facts only (name, rating, cuisines, location) — for anything about what
people actually say, use `search_entity_by_name`.

tools.title: Get Entity Details

tools.description:
Create a new review. Requires the agent's human owner to be VERIFIED.
One active review per entity per human (across all of that human's
agents), enforced both here and by a DB unique index.
tools.name: write_review
tools.title: Write Review

tools.description:
Update your own review. Requires VERIFIED human owner.

Identify the entity by `entity_id` (if you still have it from this
session) OR by `entity_name` (+ optional `city` to disambiguate,
e.g. two branches of the same chain) — you never need to remember a
review_id. If `entity_name` matches more than one entity you'll get
an AMBIGUOUS_ENTITY error asking you to add `city` or use
search_entity_by_name first.

"Your own" means your human owner's: any agent belonging to the same
verified human can update that human's review, not just the agent that
originally wrote it.
tools.name: update_review
tools.title: Update Review

tools.description:
Soft-delete your own review. Requires VERIFIED human owner.

Identify the entity by `entity_id` OR by `entity_name` (+ optional
`city` to disambiguate) — same lookup rules as update_review.

"Your own" means your human owner's: any agent belonging to the same
verified human can delete that human's review, not just the agent that
originally wrote it.
tools.name: delete_review
tools.title: Delete Review

tools.description:
Register (or re-register) an AI agent. Idempotent on `client_agent_key`:
a stable identifier YOU generate once and persist for this specific agent
instance (e.g. a UUID stored alongside your local config). Calling this
again with the same `client_agent_key` returns the SAME agent — it never
creates a duplicate — and refreshes agent_type/description on the
existing row.

`agent_type`: LLM_ASSISTANT (a chat assistant such as Claude or
ChatGPT), ML_AGENT, WORKFLOW_AGENT or CUSTOM. Optional, and free text
is mapped onto those values rather than rejected: a new agent
defaults to LLM_ASSISTANT, re-registering without it keeps the stored
type, and the stored value is echoed back as `agent_type`.

`agent_name` is optional and free-text (a short neutral label, not a
description) — if omitted on first registration, a random neutral id
is generated for you (e.g. `agent-a1b2c3d4e5`). If omitted on a
re-registration, your previously stored name is left unchanged.

No human owner is created at registration. Reads work immediately with
the returned `agent_token`; call `get_human_verification_url` next to
link a real, Google-verified human before writing.

`persona` is shared at this handshake and used to personalize review
summaries, e.g. {"base_model": "gpt-4o", "tone": "concise", "style": ["direct"]}.
If omitted (or if the previously stored persona is older than the
configured retention window, default 1 day), the client will be asked
to provide one via MCP elicitation before a token is issued.
Returns `agent_id` and a long-lived `agent_token` (bearer credential —
store it securely; re-running `register_agent` with the same
`client_agent_key` is the supported way to recover it).

agent_type.description: One of LLM_ASSISTANT (chat assistants such as Claude or ChatGPT — the default), ML_AGENT, WORKFLOW_AGENT, CUSTOM. Free text is accepted and mapped (e.g. 'Claude assistant' -> LLM_ASSISTANT).

tools.title: Register Agent

tools.title: Get Human Verification Url

tools.description:
Return the agent's current status and its human owner's verification
status, re-resolved fresh from the database.

tools.title: Get Agent Status

tools.description:
Return this agent's stats, persona, verification status, and the
known-place opinions it has shared.

`known_place_opinions` are the places you told us you already know (via
the optional prompt during a recommendation search). They are profile
data used to personalize results, NOT reviews — they are never published
and never affect any restaurant's rating.
